battle.name: 鄭文雅
battle.brief: 隋大業十年六月初五（公元614年7月16日），建安郡人林寶護、鄭文雅等聚眾數萬起義，橫行閩北，攻陷建安郡城，郡治閩縣（今福建福州）太守楊景祥敗死，是閩中首場大規模民變。時值隋煬帝第三次征高麗，丁壯遠赴遼東，攻防雙方在城垣與街巷中大量使用長矛、弓弩、雲梯與撞門之具。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的一方是隋朝在福建的行政與鎮戍體系。建安郡（郡治閩縣，今福建福州）由朝廷任命的太守楊景祥坐鎮，郡下設縣吏、縣兵與戍卒，另有由中央臨時抽調、準備北上的丁壯與運糧徭夫；郡兵一部隸屬州府，一部分置縣與津渡，負責烽燧、驛遞與城池守備。另一方是由林寶護、鄭文雅率領的閩北起義群眾，據地方志記載，參與者聚眾數萬，其中既有編戶齊民，也有依山而居的山民、俚戶與漁獵之民，隊伍沒有常設編制，靠推舉首領臨時聚合，以竹木、皮革自製器械，行動則多在郡城之外的鄉里、山地與渡口之間轉移。雙方都談不上完整建制：隋方在第三次征高麗抽走精兵、郡縣文書與錢糧之後，福建一線只剩守城兵與臨時應徵的鄉勇；起義方則只有鬥志、熟悉山道與鄉里地形兩項優勢，攻城器械與後方基地都極有限。整場衝突的本質，是隋朝州縣體系在江南最後一處仍能運作的地方，因兵源與糧源被抽空而崩解的過程。
countriesEn: One side was the Sui administrative and garrison system in Fujian. Jian'an Commandery, seated at Min County in present-day Fuzhou, Fujian, was governed by the court-appointed taishou Yang Jingxiang, with county clerks, county levies and garrison detachments beneath him, together with a share of the able-bodied men and the grain-transport corvée detached from the commandery for service in the north; part of the commandery troops were subordinated to the prefectural and provincial commands, part were distributed to the counties and the ferry stations to man the beacon towers, the courier posts and the city defences. The other side was the insurgency of the northern hills of central Fujian led by Lin Baohu and Zheng Wenyao. Local gazetteers record that several tens of thousands gathered, among them registered farming households as well as mountain-dwelling, indigenous and fishing-hunting people who lived off the uplands; there was no standing establishment, the crowd came together under self-elected leaders, its weapons were improvised from bamboo, timber and hide, and its movements ran between the hamlets, the hills and the ferry landings outside the commandery city. Neither side amounted to a proper army: once the third campaign against Goguryeo had drawn away the trained soldiers, the registers, the money and the grain, the Sui line in Fujian was reduced to garrison troops and hastily enrolled local levies, while the insurgents held only two advantages, morale and an intimate knowledge of the hill paths and of the local terrain, with almost no siege equipment and no secure rear. The conflict was in essence the collapse, in one of the last places where it still worked, of a Sui prefectural system whose manpower and grain had been stripped out.
people: 史料記載中，這場起義留下姓名的只有三人：領袖林寶護、起義的共同發動者鄭文雅，以及在城破時戰死的建安太守楊景祥。林寶護是建安郡本地人，《隋書》《北史》與地方志都把他列為首領，但關於其出身、年歲與事蹟的細節都極簡略；鄭文雅在正史中僅與林寶護並列名字，記載有限，其身分與具體所為仍待考。楊景祥是朝廷派任的建安太守，在郡城被攻破時出戰敗死。遠在遼東的隋煬帝是這一事件的最終背景人物：他於大業十年再度大舉征高麗，天下丁壯與江淮糧秣被大批抽調，閩中的起義正發生在這次徵發的高峰。另可對照的是同年隋境內相繼出現的其他起義，據《隋書·煬帝下》與相關年表，唐弼、張大彪與宗世模、劉迦論、楊公卿、司馬長安、劉苗王、王德仁、左孝友、盧明月等各自舉事，說明這不是孤立的治安事件，而是隋朝後期全國性的崩解現象。
peopleEn: Only three names attached to this rising survive in the record: the leader Lin Baohu, the co-originator Zheng Wenyao, and Yang Jingxiang, the Jian'an taishou who died when the commandery city fell. Lin Baohu was a native of Jian'an; the Sui Shu, the Bei Shi and the local gazetteer all name him as leader, but details of his birth, age and career are extremely meagre. In the official histories Zheng Wenyao appears only alongside Lin Baohu's name, so his status and his particular deeds remain matters for later research. Yang Jingxiang was the taishou appointed by the court; he chose to fight in the field and was killed in the collapse. The Sui emperor Yang Guang, then campaigning in Liaodong, is the ultimate background figure: in the tenth year of Daye he levied the country for yet another push against Goguryeo, pulling able-bodied men and grain out of Jianghuai, and the rising in Fujian came at the height of that levy. For comparison, the same year saw other revolts across Sui territory; according to the Sui Shu and the corresponding chronologies, Tang Bi, Zhang Dabiao together with Zong Shimo, Liu Jialun, Yang Gongqing, Sima Chang'an, Liu Miaowang, Wang Deren, Zuo Xiaoyou and Lu Mingyue each raised banners, which shows that this was not an isolated matter of local security but part of a general disintegration of the late Sui state.
kits: 本卡所示的埃及長矛，代表的是冷兵器體系中矛兵這一環：早王朝時期的銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。同一套技術路數經數千年傳播，落到隋代的閩中就是槊與長矛：隋軍步卒以槊、盾為主裝備，郡兵與縣兵另配環首刀、弓箭與弩，騎兵用馬槊，城守則倚靠勁弩、矢石與拒馬，遠征高麗的隊伍還攜帶用於野營的軛車與帳具。起義群眾的器械更雜，長矛多取自耕作用具、漁叉與竹木，護身多靠皮甲、藤甲與竹札甲，少數人持繩梯、竹梯作攻城之用，渡江則靠竹排與木筏。攻城方向上，雲梯、穴地、撞門之具與火燒是當時最常見的幾種手段；而在閩江上游的丘陵地帶，長矛同時是守軍拒絕登城、封堵缺口的最後一道兵器，也是起義軍破門之後在狹窄街巷中清剿殘敵的主兵器。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear shown on this card stands for the spear arm of the cold-weapons order: a copper or bronze head of the early-dynasty period bound to a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls and later to recover lost ground. The same line of technique, transmitted across several millennia, appears in Sui-era central Fujian as the shao and the long spear. Sui infantry were equipped above all with spears and shields; commandery and county levies added ring-pommel swords, bows and crossbows, cavalry used the mounted shao, the defence of walls relied on powerful crossbows, stone-throwers and caltrops, and the columns marching against Goguryeo also carried the yoke-carts and tent gear of the field camp. The insurgents' equipment was far more miscellaneous: their spears were often taken from farm tools, fishing spears and bamboo or timber, body protection came from leather, rattan and bamboo-slat armour, a few men carried rope and bamboo ladders for the assault, and ferrying was done on bamboo rafts and timber punts. In siege work the commonest devices of the day were scaling ladders, mining, battering rams and fire; and in the hilly country of the upper Min River the spear was at once the defenders' last line against boarders and the tool that sealed the breaches, and the insurgents' main weapon for clearing the cramped lanes once the gate was down.
tactics: 起義的展開依循鄉里武裝的老辦法：先在郡城之外的鄉里、山地與渡口集結人馬，掃清前哨與烽燧，切斷郡城與外縣、以及與閩江下游的聯繫，再以人數上的壓倒優勢圍逼城池。雲梯沿牆根架設，穴地與撞門同時施壓，弓弩壓制城頭守軍，逼其不敢出城；建安太守楊景祥選擇出戰，城外野戰失利後退守城垣亦告失守，郡城遂陷。守城一方的部署仍依郡兵常制：分段扼守城門與馬面，拒馬環繞缺口，弓弩手居高壓制，近衛以長矛列陣封住登城點，糧秣則靠閩江船運與城內倉廩維持。起義方在得手之後並未建立政權，也未控制沿海航運與閩江糧運，糧秣與器械只能靠繳獲與徵集維持，人數雖多卻難以久駐；數年後，隋廷自江淮與嶺北調來的援軍、以及征高麗歸來的殘兵重新集結，起義軍缺少後方與補充，最終被逐步壓制，於隋朝正式崩潰之前平定。
tacticsEn: The rising unfolded in the classic manner of a village armed rising: men first mustered in the hamlets, the hills and the ferry landings outside the commandery city, swept out the outposts and beacon stations, cut the links between the city and the outer counties as well as with the Min River below, and only then closed in with a decisive superiority in numbers. Scaling ladders were set against the foot of the wall, mining and battering proceeded at the same time, and bows and crossbows pinned the defenders on the wall so that they would not sortie. Taishou Yang Jingxiang chose to fight in the open; his defeat in the field was followed by the loss of the wall, and the commandery city fell. The defenders' deployment followed the standard pattern of commandery levies: the gates and each rampart segment were held separately, caltrops ringed the breaches, crossbowmen shot down from above, a bodyguard stood in a spear line to seal the points where boarders could land, and the food supply was kept up by river transport on the Min and by the granaries inside the walls. Having taken the city, the insurgents set up no government and controlled neither coastal shipping nor the grain traffic of the Min River; food and equipment could be maintained only from capture and requisition, and a host that was large in numbers could not be kept in place for long. Years later the relief forces the court sent from Jianghuai and Lingbei, together with the remnants returning from the Goguryeo campaign, regrouped; lacking a rear area and replacements, the insurgents were gradually worn down and were put down before the Sui dynasty's final collapse.
data: 可以確定的數字有限，但仍有幾項可供核對。起義時間記為隋大業十年六月初五辛未，即公元614年7月16日；參與首領的姓名為林寶護與鄭文雅；起義軍的規模記載為「聚眾數萬」，其兵員數、器械數與損失數在《隋書》《北史》與地方志中均無記載。建安太守楊景祥敗死一事則記載明確。同一年的背景數字反而較為豐富：隋煬帝第三次征高麗，據《資治通鑑》記載徵發天下之兵約一百一十三萬，糧秣自江淮與河北運河北上，七月屯兵懷城，遇雨久滯，兼有疫癘與糧盡，十月下令退軍，撤退途中大量士卒死亡與逃散，被後世視為隋亡的先兆之一。同一份年表還列出同年隋境內至少十數處起義，可見閩中這一支並非孤例。至於起義軍與隋軍雙方的戰損，以及攻城器械的數量，現有史料並無可信記載，本文不作推測。
dataEn: Few figures can be verified, but several are usable. The rising is dated to the fifth day of the sixth month of the tenth year of Daye, xinwei, that is 16 July 614. The names of the principal figures are Lin Baohu and Zheng Wenyao. The size of the insurgent force is recorded as 'several tens of thousands'; no figure for its numbers, its equipment or its losses survives in the Sui Shu, the Bei Shi or the local gazetteer. The record that taishou Yang Jingxiang died fighting is explicit. The background figures of the same year are better documented: for the third campaign against Goguryeo the Zizhi Tongjian records that the emperor called up roughly 1,130,000 men from across the empire, with grain shipped from Jianghuai and by the Hebei canal, that in the seventh month the army was stalled at Huaicheng amid prolonged rain, with epidemic sickness and empty granaries, and that in the tenth month the retreat was ordered, with heavy loss of life and widespread desertion on the march back, an episode long treated as a harbinger of the dynasty's end. The same chronology lists at least a dozen separate revolts in Sui territory in that year, showing that the rising in Fujian was no isolated case. Reliable figures for the losses of either side and for the number of siege devices used simply do not exist, and none are invented here.
cause: 起義的直接背景，是隋朝在第三次征高麗時對全國丁壯與錢糧的再度抽取。大業十年之前，隋煬帝已兩度征討高麗，江淮、嶺南的丁壯被大量徵發，糧船自江南運往遼東，役期長、消耗大，民間早已怨聲載道；同年再度大舉征兵，福建一線的丁壯與運役也被牽動。其次是建安郡本身的地理與治理條件：郡境內山嶺稠密，漢民、山越與俚戶雜居，郡縣對山區的控制一向薄弱，民間結社與山寨式的聚居傳統長期存在，沿海的鹽、漁之利又使豪族與鄉里首領握有資財與人望。第三是地方治理的鬆動，太守以下官吏在長期徵發與流民流動中失去對鄉里的掌控，郡兵逃亡與缺額已經明顯。於是當徵役期限延長、糧價騰貴之際，一批在鄉里素有號召力的人便以清鄉式的姿態聚眾起事，一舉攻下郡城，把對隋朝的不滿變成公開的軍事行動。
causeEn: The immediate background was the renewed extraction of able-bodied men, money and grain for the third campaign against Goguryeo. Before 614 the Sui emperor had already campaigned against Goguryeo twice, levying the men of Jianghuai and Lingnan and shipping grain from the south up to Liaodong; the service was long and ruinously costly, and resentment was already general. The levy of 614 drew in the able-bodied men and the transport corvée of Fujian as well. Second came the geography and the administrative conditions of Jian'an itself: the commandery was thick with hills, Han settlers lived mixed with mountain and indigenous populations, the prefectural authorities had always been weak in the uplands, and village associations and hill-fort habits persisted there for generations, while the salt and fishing wealth of the coast gave the great families and the local leaders both wealth and standing. Third, local government had loosened: county officials below the taishou had lost their grip over the countryside amid repeated levies and population movement, and the commandery levies were shrinking through desertion and default. So when the term of service was extended and grain prices rose, a handful of men with standing in their own districts gathered a following and rose in arms; the capture of the commandery city turned a widespread grievance into open military action.
impact: 這場起義的意義，首先在於它是閩中第一次大規模的公開民變；在此之前，福建是隋朝最後一片維持表面秩序的江南之地，郡縣文書、賦稅與漕運尚能照常下達。起義一旦攻破郡城、建安太守戰死，等於宣告州縣體系在東南的崩解：閩江下游的秩序中斷，郡兵與縣吏各自為守，朝廷不得不自江淮與嶺北抽調兵馬回援，而當時的隋朝正把主力壓在遼東前線，調度已無餘裕。更深一層的影響在政治心理上——同年唐弼、劉迦論、楊公卿、司馬長安、劉苗王、王德仁、左孝友、盧明月等起義相繼出現，證明「郡兵反正、聚眾破城」是一條可複製的路子，各地首領由此看見推翻隋朝的可能性，隋廷的威信與徵召能力在這一年被連續削弱。從長時段看，閩中此後仍有汪文進、蔡道助等相繼舉事，直到唐末王審知兄弟入閩，福建再度成為割據的落腳點之一，隋末這場起義可算是這條脈絡的早期一環。
impactEn: The significance of the rising lies first in its being the first large-scale open rebellion in central Fujian. Until then Fujian was the last part of the south where the Sui order still appeared to function, with registers, taxes and canal shipments still going out on schedule. Once the commandery city fell and its taishou was killed, the collapse of the prefectural system in the southeast was announced: the order of the lower Min River was interrupted, commandery troops and county clerks each held what they could, and the court was forced to recall troops from Jianghuai and Lingbei at a moment when the Sui had its main body committed in Liaodong and no reserves to spare. The deeper effect was political and psychological: the appearance in the same year of the risings of Tang Bi, Liu Jialun, Yang Gongqing, Sima Chang'an, Liu Miaowang, Wang Deren, Zuo Xiaoyou and Lu Mingyue showed that 'the levies turn, the crowd takes the city' was a repeatable path, and local leaders across the empire could see for themselves the possibility of bringing the Sui down, while the court's prestige and its capacity to levy men were worn down in that single year. Over the long run further risings followed in central Fujian, among them those of Wang Wenjin and Cai Daozhu, and Fujian was to become one of the resting places of later separatist regimes until Wang Shenzhi and his brothers entered the province at the end of the Tang. This Sui rising can be read as an early link in that chain.
result: 就戰役本身而言，結果是起義軍一度得手：隋大業十年六月初五，林寶護、鄭文雅聚眾數萬，橫行閩北，攻陷建安郡城，建安太守楊景祥出戰敗死，郡治閩縣落入起義者手中，這是閩中第一次出現攻下郡城、斬殺太守的規模。但起義沒有能力把勝利轉為政權：既未在所據之地建立戶口與糧秣徵收，也未控制閩江航運與沿海海口，攻城所耗的器械無法補充，部隊缺乏後方基地與指揮體系的固定化。隋廷自江淮、嶺北調集的援軍抵達後，與地方鎮戍及豪族武裝合流，逐步收復郡縣；起義餘部退入山地，繼續以小股形式抗爭，又在隋朝正式崩潰之前被平定，閩中重歸朝廷控制，郡縣秩序恢復得並不徹底，此後數年仍不斷有零星起事。這場戰役的直接結果，是隋朝在福建的統治更加依賴鎮戍與地方勢力；而它留下的教訓，則是隋廷已無力同時應付高麗戰線與國內的崩解。
resultEn: As a campaign, the immediate outcome was a limited success for the insurgents. On the fifth day of the sixth month of the tenth year of Daye, Lin Baohu and Zheng Wenyao gathered several tens of thousands, moved through the hills north of the Min, took the city of Jian'an Commandery, and killed taishou Yang Jingxiang, who had chosen to fight in the field; the seat at Min County passed into the hands of the insurgents, the first time in central Fujian that a commandery city had been taken and a taishou killed on that scale. But the rising could not convert that victory into a regime. It set up neither a population register nor a grain collection in the territory it held, it did not control navigation on the Min River or the coastal ports, the siege devices it had consumed could not be replaced, and the force lacked a rear area and any fixed chain of command. When the relief armies gathered by the court from Jianghuai and Lingbei arrived, they joined the local garrisons and the armed strength of the great families and recovered county after county; the remnants withdrew into the hills and carried on resistance in small bands until they were suppressed before the Sui dynasty's formal end, and central Fujian returned to nominal court control, though the restoration of order was never thorough and sporadic risings continued for several years. The direct result was that Sui rule in Fujian henceforth relied even more heavily on garrisons and on local power, and the lesson left behind was that the court could no longer fight on two fronts at once, against Goguryeo and against its own dissolving state.
